title: In Guangzhou, Breakfast Lasts 3 Hours — Cantonese Yum Cha | China Travel Expert
description:
In Guangzhou, breakfast isn't a rushed coffee — it can stretch to three hours.

Cantonese call it yum cha, "drink tea," and the rule is 一盅两件: one pot of tea, two small plates — steamer towers of har gow, char siu bao and egg tarts. Watch the locals: when someone refills your cup, they tap two fingers on the table. It's a silent thank-you, a "finger kowtow" tied to a Qianlong-era legend. The whole ritual grew out of Qing-dynasty Guangzhou, when the city was China's one trading port — and in 2007 it was named an intangible cultural heritage of Guangzhou.

🧭 Expert Tip: Go before 9am while the steamers are freshest, order har gow with a pot of pu'er, and tap two fingers to say thanks when your tea is poured.
